audit.whatIsWrong: The content level chart gives Mel 5 of 7 stages and Tahm Kench 0, in a matchup Tahm Kench wins 59.48%. It also contradicts the file's own prose: spikes[2] says first item 'flips the survival equation' while win[5] still reads Mel, and spikes[3] says 2+ items makes 'the FAVOURED verdict real' while win[6] reads Skill.
audit.why: A chart with zero Tahm Kench stages tells the player he loses every phase of a lane he wins overall. The lane genuinely is Mel-sided early; the scaling half is not.
audit.corrected: win[5] Mel -> Skill (matches spikes[2]); win[6] Skill -> Tahm Kench (matches spikes[3] and whys[6]). Final shape Mel 4 / Skill 2 / Tahm Kench 1 — lane lost, game won.
sources: packet defect: level chart contradicts data

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer calls Mel's reflect her R, in five places ('Mel's R reflect', 'never fire Tongue Lash into her R', 'watch the R reflect', 'her mirror'). The reflect is Rebuttal, her W. Her R is Golden Eclipse, a global Overwhelm-scaling nuke. It also calls her 'W and E execute tools' — the execute lives on her passive Searing Brilliance (Overwhelm) and on Golden Eclipse, not on W/E.
audit.why: A player told to fear her R while poking will hold Tongue Lash for the wrong ability and eat the actual one. Rebuttal is a 250-range self-buff on a 38s rank-1 cooldown; Golden Eclipse is global with no dodge.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal (W) prevents her taking damage — a Tongue Lash into it lands for nothing and gives no An Acquired Taste stack, and it is 38/35/33/29/26s, the longest cooldown in her kit. Golden Eclipse (R) is the level-6 threat and it scales off the Overwhelm her poke has already stacked on you.
sources: champ-data/_kits/mel.json W Rebuttal, R Golden Eclipse, P Searing Brilliance

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere says that Tongue Lash's 3-stack stun and Devour compete for the same three An Acquired Taste stacks. Both layers instead teach them as one combo ('the 3-stack stun into Devour', 'When it is down — 3-stack Q stun + Devour', tradeGood, dosFull).
audit.why: Tongue Lash on a 3-stack target stuns and consumes the stacks; Devour on an enemy champion requires three stacks. Spending them on the stun removes the Devour option in the same window. The data currently instructs a sequence the kit does not permit.
audit.corrected: Three stacks buys a Q-stun or a Devour, never both — decide before you press Q.
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json P 'At three stacks, he can use Devour on an enemy champion'; Q 'they are stunned and the stacks are consumed'

audit.whatIsWrong: The tank plan ('sit behind minions and let Thick Skin grey-health her poke') is presented as free. It is not, against this specific enemy.
audit.why: Searing Brilliance applies Overwhelm on every instance of Mel's damage and the stacks accumulate without limit; Golden Eclipse then hits every Overwhelm-marked enemy anywhere on the map for damage scaled per stack. Absorbing her poke literally loads her ultimate.
audit.corrected: Eating Radiant Volley to bank grey health is loading Golden Eclipse — break combat and reset health between fights instead of carrying chip into them.
sources: champ-data/_kits/mel.json P Searing Brilliance, R Golden Eclipse

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid and whys[3]/whys[4] say Tahm Kench has 'no escape until Abyssal Voyage at 6'. Abyssal Voyage is not in his kit — it is the pre-rework ultimate.
audit.why: His reposition is Abyssal Dive (W), which is available from level 2 and is a knockup engage, not a level-6 escape. The advice tells the player to play scared for four levels holding a tool he already has.
audit.corrected: Abyssal Dive (W) is up from level 2 on a 21/20/19/18/17s cooldown; level 6 gives Devour (R).
sources: champ-data/_kits/tahmkench.json W Abyssal Dive, R Devour

audit.whatIsWrong: No real cooldown numbers anywhere in the content layer; the packet flags zero sequencing cues for this matchup.
audit.why: 'Trade when her ability is down' is unusable without the length of the window.
audit.corrected: Solar Snare 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s is the root to dodge. Rebuttal 38/35/33/29/26s is the real punish window — nothing else in her kit stops damage. Radiant Volley 10/9/8/7/6s. Your Tongue Lash is 7s at rank 1 and 900 range; Abyssal Dive 21s.

audit.why: Heartsteel first-item and the 2-item front-line window are already the stated spikes and match the scaling story. Only the chart disagreed with them, which point 2 fixes.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer refers to Mel as 'him'/'his' throughout (enemyWin, tldr, phases[4].why, breakdown.late, breakdown.feeding) while the content layer uses 'she'/'her'.
audit.why: Mel is female; the two layers render on the same page and disagree.
audit.corrected: Fixed in the strings this proposal already touches. The remainder are listed in notes — they are shared boilerplate and cannot be targeted uniquely.

edits.before: Mel's ranged Q poke is relentless at level 1 and you have no reliable way to stack An Acquired Taste through it without eating free damage — sit at max Tongue Lash range, last-hit cleanly, and let Thick Skin do its job passively. The moment she uses her Q to zone you off a cannon, that is your window to walk forward and land a Tongue Lash; one hit puts you at one stack toward the stun. Never use your Q into her R — if she has the reflect active and your skillshot hits it, she gets a free window to punish you while you are without your stun. The game plan at levels 1-3 is survival, stack fishing, and refusing to give her a kill.
edits.after: Radiant Volley is relentless at level 1 and you have no clean way to stack An Acquired Taste through it — sit at max Tongue Lash range of 900, last-hit, and let Thick Skin bank the chip. The moment she spends Radiant Volley to zone you off a cannon you have a 10-second window at rank 1: walk up and land Tongue Lash, which puts you one stack toward the stun and heals you. Never throw it into Rebuttal — her W prevents her taking damage, so the hit gives you no stack and you wait out the 7s Tongue Lash cooldown for nothing. Levels 1-3 are survival, stack fishing, and refusing to give her a kill.

edits.before: Levels 4 through 6 are Mel's strongest window — she has range, zoning, and her W and E execute tools coming online, while your kit requires getting into melee range to stack An Acquired Taste, and you have no escape until Abyssal Voyage at 6. Respect her damage here and play for CS rather than forcing trades you cannot win without landing a clean Tongue Lash first. At 6 your job shifts: Abyssal Voyage gives you global repositioning, but more importantly it signals to her that you can leave the lane and be useful elsewhere — that threat alone limits her roam windows. Still watch the R reflect every time you throw a Tongue Lash; she will bait you into throwing it into her mirror and follow up with her execute tools.
edits.after: Levels 4 through 6 are Mel's strongest window — she has range, Solar Snare's root to lock you in place, and Overwhelm piling up on your bar, while your kit needs melee range to stack An Acquired Taste. Your reposition is Abyssal Dive and it is up from level 2, not 6 — treat its knockup as the engage rather than an escape you saved too long. Play for CS unless Solar Snare is on its 11-second cooldown, and count Radiant Volley too: 10s at rank 1. At 6 you get Devour, but she gets Golden Eclipse, which fires from anywhere and scales off every Overwhelm stack her poke has stuck on you. Watch Rebuttal every time you commit; her W blanks the damage and the An Acquired Taste stack behind it, and at 38 seconds it is the best thing you can bait out of her.

edits.before: Mel cannot deal with a properly stacked 3-passive Devour in a teamfight — she simply ceases to exist for the swallow duration, and your team has a free 4v5 or a kill if she is already damaged. Your 59.48% win rate is built entirely on this: she wins the lane phase comfortably, but you win the game. Once Heartsteel and a second tank item are online, her poke no longer threatens you through Thick Skin and grey health recovery, and your point-and-click lockdown removes her from every teamfight she tries to use her kit in. Stack passively, survive the lane, and let the 25-minute team fight be your payoff.

notes: SYSTEMIC, CHAMPION-WIDE: 'Abyssal Voyage' appears 182 times across 62 of the 71 entries in champ-data/content/tahmkench.js. It is Tahm Kench's pre-rework ultimate and is not in the current kit (Data Dragon 16.15.1: W = Abyssal Dive, R = Devour). Most occurrences are of the form 'no escape until Abyssal Voyage at 6', which is wrong twice over — the reposition is W and it is available from level 2. The full layer never uses the name, so the two layers disagree with each other. This needs a champion-wide pass beyond this slice. SECOND SYSTEMIC ISSUE: both layers teach '3-stack stun into Devour' as a single combo across many matchups (tradeGood and dontsFull[2].d alone repeat the same string 4x and 280x respectively across the full file). Per the kit, Tongue Lash on a 3-stack target 'stuns and the stacks are consumed', while Devour on an enemy champion requires three stacks — they are alternatives, not a sequence. I could only fix the uniquely-addressable copies here. THIRD: the full layer calls Mel 'him/his' in shared boilerplate I could not target uniquely — breakdown.feeding, breakdown.trading, tradeGood, tradeBad, report[3].t, report[12].t all still say 'he'/'him' for a female champion. No WKM_LINES errors observed for this matchup.
